summary: Performance and security hardening driven by a new k6 load-testing pass on mymatasan. (1) Authentication throughput: because the SPA replays its HTTP Basic credential on every request, each authenticated API call previously ran a full bcrypt password comparison plus a LastLoginAt database write, capping throughput at roughly cores/bcrypt-cost regardless of endpoint. Authenticate now caches a successful verification for 30s (keyed by username + a hash of the password) so a repeated identical credential skips both the bcrypt work and the write; only successes are cached (a wrong password always pays bcrypt, so credential guessing stays expensive and the cache size is bounded by the real user count), and the cache is flushed on every user mutation (self password change, admin reset, role/active toggle, delete) so a rotated or deactivated credential stops working immediately. Measured effect on a 24-core host: steady 50-user read load p95 43.6ms -> 3.8ms, and peak throughput under stress 317 -> 764 req/s with p95 1.0s -> 256ms, zero errors. (2) Capacity endpoint: GET /api/capacity re-probed static GPU hardware on every call by spawning powershell (CIM query) and nvidia-smi, taking ~3.1s per request; the GPU device probe (also used by the Settings decoder device list and auto-tune) is now served from a 5-minute stale-while-revalidate cache, so only the first call after startup blocks and later calls return in ~0.26s (~12x faster) while a background goroutine refreshes. (3) Rate-limiter proxy trust: X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP were trusted unconditionally, letting a directly-reachable client spoof the header to mint unlimited rate-limit buckets and bypass both the global rate limiter and the login lockout (which share this client-IP keying). A new optional rateLimit.trustedProxies config (list of IPs/CIDRs) means those forwarding headers are honored only when the direct peer is a configured trusted proxy; otherwise the real peer address is used. A new tools/k6/ dev-tooling directory (k6 + Grafana + InfluxDB load-test stack with smoke/load/stress scripts) supports repeatable load tests; it is developer tooling only, like tools/zaproxy and tools/tgbridge, with no shipped-app doc coverage.
compatibility: Backward compatible for every existing install, no database migration and no required config changes. rateLimit.trustedProxies defaults to empty, which means forwarding headers are ignored and the direct peer address is used for rate limiting and login-lockout keying — the secure default; operators running mymatasan behind a reverse proxy should set it to the proxy's address(es) to restore per-client rate-limit granularity. The 30s auth-verification cache is transparent: a live password change is applied immediately (the cache is flushed on the change), and any other account state change (deactivation, role edit) also flushes the cache, so the only bounded staleness is at most 30s for an out-of-band database edit. The GPU-probe cache reflects hardware changes within 5 minutes (or on restart), which is fine for static host hardware.
